analysis: The relative-position-bias trial executed successfully but did not improve validation HR@10. Authoritative host macro HR@10 was 0.4838, versus the supplied current reference of 0.485 (−0.0012) and baseline of 0.505 (−0.0212). Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.520, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.535, Electronics 0.375, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.505. Electronics had the lowest absolute score; prior per-category scores are unavailable here, so category-level changes cannot be established. This result does not support relative-distance bias as an improvement under the retained training setup, but does not establish why performance declined. The host reported success and allocated 404.397 GPU-seconds.
code_summary: One independently trained SASRec per category, with exactly one selected checkpoint loaded for each route. Each network uses 96-dimensional tied item embeddings, learned absolute positions, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, dropout 0.3, and a jointly trained item bias. Each block adds a zero-initialized [32, heads] relative-position bias table: exact distances 0–15, then 16 logarithmic buckets through distance 127, clipping longer distances. Additive SDPA masks preserve causality, key padding, and safe diagonals for padded queries; padded outputs are zeroed. Training retains endpoint-weighted sampled softmax, 2048 shared sampled negatives, a 2048-token cap, AdamW, warmup, seed 42, and validation-based checkpoint selection with an NDCG tie-breaker. Checkpoint metadata and strict loading preserve predictor architecture parity. RNG-preserving checks cover masking, buckets, zero-bias equivalence, causality, padding, gradients, and checkpoint reload scores. No ensembles or separately fitted scoring components are used.
